{{Improve categories|date=September 2025}}{{format footnotes |date=May 2024}}
In [[mathematics]], in particular in [[computer algebra|computational algebra]], the '''Berlekamp&ndash;Zassenhaus algorithm''' is an [[algorithm]] for factoring [[polynomial]]s over the [[integer]]s, named after [[Elwyn Berlekamp]] and [[Hans Zassenhaus]]. As a consequence of [[Gauss's lemma (number theory)|Gauss's lemma]], this amounts to solving the problem also over the rationals.

The algorithm starts by finding factorizations over suitable [[finite field]]s using [[Hensel's lemma]] to lift the solution from modulo a prime&nbsp;''p'' to a convenient power of&nbsp;''p''. After this the right factors are found as a subset of these. The worst case of this algorithm is exponential in the number of factors.

Van Hoeij (2002)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=van Hoeij |first=M |date=August 2002 |title=Factoring Polynomials and the Knapsack Problem |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0022314X01927635 |journal=Journal of Number Theory |volume=95 |issue=2 |pages=167–189 |doi=10.1016/S0022-314X(01)92763-5|url-access=subscription }}</ref> improved this algorithm by using the [[LLL algorithm]], substantially reducing the time needed to choose the right subsets of mod&nbsp;''p'' factors.
